question.problem:
The joint CDF of two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y,$ for $(x,y)\in [0,\frac{\pi }{2}]\times [0,\frac{\pi }{2}],$ is given by

$$
F(x,y)=\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{sin}⁡y-\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y)).
$$

Find ${F}_{Y}(y),$ the marginal CDF of $Y,$ for $0\le y\le \frac{\pi }{2}.$
question.worked_solution:
The marginal CDF of $X$ is given by

$$
{F}_{Y}(y)=F(\infty ,y)={lim}_{x\to \infty }F(x,y).
$$

Therefore, for $0\le y\le \frac{\pi }{2},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{F}_{Y}(y) & =F(\infty ,y) \\  & =F(\frac{\pi }{2},y) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{\pi }{2}+\operatorname{sin}⁡y-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}+y)) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(1+\operatorname{sin}⁡y-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}+y)) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(1+\operatorname{sin}⁡y-\operatorname{cos}⁡y)\end{aligned}
$$
